lead: A locus diagram is the path traced by the tip of a phasor when one circuit quantity is varied and the source voltage is held fixed. For series RL, RC and RLC circuits the current traces part of a circle, so one sketch shows the largest current, the power factor at every setting, the value for maximum power, and the settings that make a parallel circuit resonate. Some syllabi place locus diagrams with AC circuit analysis rather than with resonance.
prereq: You need: phasors, impedance and admittance, and the resonance condition from series resonance and parallel resonance.

blocks.text: Take the supply voltage V as the reference phasor, along the positive real axis. In a series circuit I = V/Z. If only R changes, Z = R + jX keeps its imaginary part, so the tip of Z moves along a horizontal line; if only X changes, it moves along a vertical line at distance R.

The current is V times the inverse of that line, and a straight line that misses the origin inverts into a circle through the origin. Only the part reached by positive values of the varied element is drawn.
To draw a current locus in an exam:

items: Draw V along the horizontal axis; lagging currents go below it, leading currents above it.
Find the end points: the current when the varied element is zero and when it is infinite.
Draw the semicircle on the diameter V/(fixed element), below V for an inductive circuit, above for a capacitive one.
Check one middle point by calculating V/Z.

blocks.text: Series RL with R varied and X<sub>L</sub> fixed. With θ the angle by which the current lags V, tan θ = X<sub>L</sub>/R and |I| = V/√(R² + X<sub>L</sub>²) = (V/X<sub>L</sub>) sin θ. In polar form this is a circle of diameter V/X<sub>L</sub> whose diameter lies along the −90° axis. At R = 0 the current is V/X<sub>L</sub> at −90°; as R → ∞ it shrinks to zero along the V axis. The power P = VI cos θ is the horizontal coordinate of the tip, so it is largest at the right-most point of the semicircle, where θ = 45° and R = X<sub>L</sub>.
|I| = (V/XL) sin θ (R varied), |I| = (V/R) cos θ (XL varied)
Here θ is the angle between I and V; the first is a circle of diameter V/X<sub>L</sub> on the −90° axis, the second a circle of diameter V/R on the V axis.
Series RL with X<sub>L</sub> varied and R fixed. Now |I| = (V/R) cos θ, a circle of diameter V/R on the V axis: from V/R in phase at X<sub>L</sub> = 0, round the lower half toward the origin.
In every case the diameter is V over the fixed element, and the 45° point is where the varied element equals the fixed one.

sections.h3: Series RLC with frequency varied, and parallel branches

blocks.text: In a series RLC circuit with R fixed, the net reactance X = ωL − 1/(ωC) runs from −∞ to +∞ as ω rises from 0 to ∞. So the current traces the whole circle of diameter V/R on the V axis. Below ω₀ the circuit is capacitive and the tip is on the upper (leading) half; at ω₀ it reaches I = V/R in phase with V; above ω₀ it is on the lower half. The half-power frequencies are the two points at ±45°, where |I| = V/(R√2).

In a parallel circuit the branch currents add. If one branch is fixed (for example a capacitor carrying I<sub>C</sub> = V/X<sub>C</sub> at +90°), the total current locus is the varied branch's semicircle shifted by I<sub>C</sub>. Wherever the shifted circle crosses the V axis, the total current is in phase with V: the circuit is resonant.

For a coil branch R + jX<sub>L</sub> across a capacitor X<sub>C</sub>, the susceptances cancel when X<sub>L</sub>/(R² + X<sub>L</sub>²) = 1/X<sub>C</sub>. With X<sub>L</sub> varied this gives X<sub>L</sub>² − X<sub>C</sub> X<sub>L</sub> + R² = 0: two resonant values of X<sub>L</sub> if X<sub>C</sub> > 2R, one if X<sub>C</sub> = 2R, none if X<sub>C</sub> < 2R. With R varied it gives R² = X<sub>L</sub>(X<sub>C</sub> − X<sub>L</sub>), one value, which exists only when X<sub>C</sub> > X<sub>L</sub>.

figure.caption: Left: the first worked example. With X<sub>L</sub> = 10 Ω and 100 V, the current tip runs round a semicircle of diameter 10 A below V as R rises; the right-most point, R = 10 Ω, gives the maximum power of 500 W. Right: the second example. The coil current circle (dashed) moves up by the 10 A capacitor current and cuts the V axis at 3.33 A and 30 A, the two resonant settings.

spec.aria: Two current locus diagrams: a semicircle of diameter 10 amps for a series RL circuit with variable resistance, with points for R equal to 0, 5, 10, 20 and 40 ohms, and a coil current circle shifted up by 10 amps that crosses the voltage axis at 3.33 and 30 amps.

examples.question: A series RL circuit has X<sub>L</sub> = 10 Ω and a variable resistor R, fed from 100 V. Draw the current locus, find the current for R = 0, 5, 10, 20 and 40 Ω, and find the value of R for maximum power and that power.
steps: Fixed element X<sub>L</sub> = 10 Ω, so the diameter is V/X<sub>L</sub> = 100/10 = 10 A, along the −90° axis. Centre at 5 A below the origin.
R = 0: I = 100/(j10) = 10∠−90° A, the bottom of the circle.
R = 10 Ω: I = 100/(10 + j10) = 7.07∠−45° A = 5 − j5 A, the right-most point.
Check that the points lie on the circle: 4 − j8 is √(4² + 3²) = 5 A from the centre (0, −5); so are 5 − j5 and 4 − j2.
Power P = V × Re(I) is largest at the right-most point, R = X<sub>L</sub> = 10 Ω: P = 100 × 5 = 500 W = V²/(2X<sub>L</sub>).
examples.answer: The locus is a semicircle of diameter 10 A below V; the currents are 10, 8.94, 7.07, 4.47 and 2.43 A; maximum power 500 W at R = 10 Ω.

examples.question: A coil branch of R = 3 Ω in series with a variable inductance is connected in parallel with a capacitor of X<sub>C</sub> = 10 Ω across 100 V, 50 Hz. Find the values of L that give resonance and the supply current in each case.
steps: Resonance condition: X<sub>L</sub>² − X<sub>C</sub> X<sub>L</sub> + R² = 0, that is X<sub>L</sub>² − 10X<sub>L</sub> + 9 = 0.
X<sub>C</sub> = 10 Ω > 2R = 6 Ω, so there are two roots: X<sub>L</sub> = (10 ± √(100 − 36))/2 = (10 ± 8)/2 = 9 Ω or 1 Ω.
For X<sub>L</sub> = 9 Ω: coil current 100/(3 + j9) = 3.33 − j10 A; adding I<sub>C</sub> = j10 A gives 3.33 A in phase with V.
For X<sub>L</sub> = 1 Ω: coil current 100/(3 + j1) = 30 − j10 A; adding j10 A gives 30 A in phase with V.
On the locus: the coil current traces a semicircle of diameter V/R = 33.3 A; shifted up by 10 A it cuts the V axis at 3.33 A and 30 A.
examples.answer: L = 28.6 mH (supply current 3.33 A) or L = 3.18 mH (supply current 30 A).

traps: The impedance locus with R varied is a straight line, but the current locus is a circle. Do not draw the current as a line.
Diameter slip: with R varied the diameter is V/X; with X varied it is V/R. The diameter is always V over the element that stays fixed.
Half-plane: an RL current lags and is drawn below V; an RC current leads and is drawn above V. A locus on the wrong side earns no marks.
Two resonant values of X<sub>L</sub> exist only when X<sub>C</sub> > 2R. Check the discriminant before quoting two answers.
Maximum power with R varied comes at R = |X| (the 45° point), and P<sub>max</sub> = V²/(2|X|); it is not at R = 0, where the current is largest.

quiz.a: The path traced by the tip of a phasor, usually the current, when one circuit parameter or the frequency varies while the supply voltage is fixed.

quiz.q: Why is the current locus of a series RL circuit with variable R a semicircle and not a straight line?
quiz.a: Z = R + jX<sub>L</sub> moves on a straight line, and I = V/Z is its inverse; inverting a line that misses the origin gives a circle through the origin. Only R ≥ 0 is drawn, so a semicircle.

quiz.q: A series RC circuit has X<sub>C</sub> = 25 Ω and variable R, on 50 V. Find the diameter of the current locus and the maximum power.
quiz.a: Diameter V/X<sub>C</sub> = 50/25 = 2 A on the +90° axis. Maximum power at R = 25 Ω: I = 50/(25√2) = 1.414 A at +45°, P = 1.414² × 25 = 50 W = V²/(2X<sub>C</sub>).

quiz.q: A series RLC circuit with R = 10 Ω is fed from 10 V and the frequency is varied. Give the diameter of the current circle and the current at the half-power points.
quiz.a: Diameter V/R = 1 A on the V axis (the current at resonance). At the half-power points the current is 1/√2 = 0.707 A, at +45° and −45°.

quiz.q: A coil of R = 3 Ω and variable X<sub>L</sub> is in parallel with X<sub>C</sub> = 5 Ω. How many values of X<sub>L</sub> give resonance?
quiz.a: X<sub>L</sub>² − 5X<sub>L</sub> + 9 = 0 has discriminant 25 − 36 < 0, so none. On the locus, the coil circle of diameter V/3 shifted up by V/5 never reaches the V axis, because V/5 is more than its radius V/6.

beyond: Not for the exam. The same circle idea gives the circle diagram of an induction motor and the power circle diagram of a transmission line. The Smith chart of radio-frequency design and the Nyquist plot of feedback control are locus charts too. Search next: induction motor circle diagram, Smith chart, Nyquist plot.
